items.title: Buddy DeFranco interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: When we actually met in the 50s and played together at the Jazz at the Philharmonic. Night after night. And recorded several albums before together

ctx.x: This is funny because Norman decided that since so much time had passed, he decided to title this “Buddy DeFranco meets the Oscar Peterson Quartet.” When we actually met in the 50s and played together at the Jazz at the Philharmonic. Night after night. And recorded several albums before together, including one of my favorites, the “George Gershwin Songbook.” Russ Garcia arrangements, the big orchestra, that’s one of the nicest. But this was fun. It’s always fun to work with Oscar. Always. Because he’s so dynamic…
Interesting statement. How to play for the clarinet.

items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Life-long friends and we did a lot of recordings together

ctx.x: And then you became life-long friends and …

Life-long friends and we did a lot of recordings together, and I wanted to do a Gershwin album with Oscar and I approached Norman Granz with the idea. And this meant with strings, a big orchestra, maybe thirty pieces, twenty-seven …” and he said, “absolutely not, no.” He said, “I’d like you to stay with the small group.” I went to Oscar and I said, “Oscar, I’d like to do this Gershwin album with you, with a big orchestra” and Oscar said, “yeah, great.” I said, “but Norman doesn’t want to be part of it.” He said,…
